page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Point mutation defined
steps.margin_note: Definition, the other name, and the three kinds. Five lines.
lines: A POINT MUTATION is a mutation that occurs in a
It is also called a gene mutation.
It may be a substitution, an insertion or a
steps.why: Because only one base changes, the change can be traced through to one amino acid and one protein.
common_mistakes: Saying it affects the whole gene. It affects ONE base pair.
Confusing it with a chromosomal mutation, which changes chromosome number or structure.
steps.memory_tip: A single point on the DNA.

steps.label: Example
steps.margin_note: Name it, give the codon change, the amino acid change, and the result.

lines.text: Sickle cell anaemia: GAG becomes GTG

lines: In the gene for the beta chain of haemoglobin,
one base changes: GAG becomes GTG.
So GLUTAMIC ACID is replaced by VALINE at
The red blood cell then becomes sickle shaped.
steps.why: One base, one codon, one amino acid, one cell shape: this is the clearest chain from a DNA change to a visible symptom in the whole syllabus.
common_mistakes: Naming a chromosomal disorder such as Down's syndrome. That is not a point mutation.
Saying valine is replaced by glutamic acid. It is the other way round: GLUTAMIC ACID is replaced by VALINE at position 6.
steps.memory_tip: One letter changes and the cell changes shape.
